name: ACS724LLCTR-10AU-T
title: ACS724: automotive Hall-effect current sensor, 1.2 mΩ isolated conductor, differential sensing, SOIC-8
summary: A current sensor in an 8-pin SOIC: the current runs through a 1.2 mΩ copper path on pins 1-2 to 3-4, and a pair of Hall plates under it turns the field into a 5 V ratiometric analog voltage on VIOUT, with the difference of the two plates cancelling a uniform outside field. The sensing side (pins 5 to 8) is isolated from the conductor, rated 2400 Vrms for 60 s, so it can sit on a high-side line. Bandwidth is 120 kHz, reduced with a capacitor on FILTER. Parts span 2.5 A to 50 A, unidirectional (output 0.1 × VCC at zero) or bidirectional (0.5 × VCC); ACS724LLCTR-10AU-T is the 0 to 10 A, 400 mV/A unidirectional part with Pb-based solder bumps. AEC-Q100 qualified.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensed current enters at pins 1-2 and leaves at pins 3-4; VIOUT moves with it. VCC is decoupled to GND with 0.1 µF. A 1 nF CF from FILTER to GND narrows the bandwidth for lower noise. CLOAD is whatever capacitance the output drives.

operation.text: Current in the copper path makes a field that two Hall plates on the die read. The output is their difference, so a uniform outside field largely cancels (CMFRR 40 dB typ). The Hall front end is chopper-stabilized and the sensitivity and zero-current output are trimmed after packaging; temperature drift is corrected digitally. An internal shield between the conductor and the die keeps fast voltage swings on the conductor out of the output. Magnetic hysteresis is close to zero.

VIOUT rises as current goes from pins 1-2 to pins 3-4. At zero current it sits at 0.5 × VCC on AB (bidirectional) parts, 2.5 V at VCC = 5 V, and at 0.1 × VCC on AU (unidirectional) parts. Both sensitivity and zero-current output scale with VCC. Sensitivity is the product of the coupling from current to field (G/A, with 1 G = 0.1 mT) and the amplifier gain (mV/G), set at the factory for each range.

Voltage offset error is the zero-current output's departure from 0.5 × VCC or 0.1 × VCC from non-magnetic causes; divided by Sens it is in amperes. Total output error folds in every source: near full scale it is mostly sensitivity error, near zero current mostly offset, and it goes to infinity at IP = 0.

Small-signal bandwidth is 120 kHz typ with CL = 1 nF. The FILTER pin connects to an internal 1.8 kΩ resistor; a capacitor from FILTER to GND forms a low-pass with it. With CF = 4.7 nF the bandwidth is 18 kHz and input-referred noise 25 mA(rms) typ.

Response time runs from the input current reaching 90 % of its final value to the output reaching 90 % of full scale. Propagation delay is the same at 20 %. Rise time is the output's 10 % to 90 % interval, and slew rate the output's rate of change across that interval.

While the supply climbs the part holds in power-on reset, then starts once VCC is high enough to keep it running. tPO is the time from VCC reaching VCC(min) to the output settling within ±10 % of its final value with a field applied; 80 µs typ.

The conductor pins 1-4 are galvanically isolated from the signal pins 5-8, so the part can measure high-side current without a differential amplifier. Creepage and clearance are 4.2 mm each; a slot in the board under the package keeps 4.2 mm creepage once mounted.

Die temperature rises with current through the conductor, depending on board copper, cooling and the current's peak, on-time and duty cycle. Measured with DC at TA = 25 °C on the ASEK724 board (TED-85-0740-003: 1500 mm² of 4 oz, 0.1388 mm, copper on pins 1-2 and on pins 3-4, thermal vias), the rise in die temperature holds at other ambient temperatures and approximates the rise for AC and pulsed currents. Currents above the continuous limit are allowed as long as TJ stays at or below 165 °C.

Flip-chip die in an SOIC-8 with a 100 % matte tin leadframe. -S parts use tin-silver solder bumps and are Pb-free without exemptions; -T parts use Pb-based bumps and are RoHS-compliant under Annex III and IV exemptions 7(a), 15 and 15(a) of Directive 2011/65/EU. The two perform the same. AEC-Q100 qualified.
The branded face carries the part number, package designator and temperature range, the amperage variant, and the lot number; the country of origin is on the underside.
